plan.purpose: Attribute current complete reused-browser application lifetimes to original Flashwright engine request intervals before selecting a native coarse-action experiment.

matrix.order: Applications and profiles reversed in second block

plan.mechanism: Passive wrapper of EngineClient.request records method, action, original page/context identity, native CLOCK_MONOTONIC start/end and rejection; no callbacks or browser commands are inserted. Records retained at process exit.
plan.verification: Unchanged original test bodies and HTTP inventory; native original browser waits/journals and fresh-context worker reports; join complete request stream to actual worker and outer original clock. Merge overlapping request intervals instead of summing elapsed time.
plan.scope: Diagnostic intervals include IPC, queueing, application and browser waiting, and cleanup. Not CPU attribution, exact critical-path causality, removable-time bounds or a new speed comparison.
plan.resourcePolicy: Serial systemd units with CPUQuota400%,MemoryMax8G,zero swap; artifacts off, retries0.
plan.decisionRule: Use the observed phase distribution to choose the next attribution boundary. Do not infer a coarse endpoint gain by subtracting request intervals or independent-clock spans.

analysis.scope: Union of measured request intervals, not CPU or a removable-cost estimate. Native clock shares original watchdog domain. Test bodies and selected recorded worker outcomes verified.

plan.purpose: Observe native trace intervals within the current full-capability reused-browser original suite.
plan.runs: Four Flashwright worker1 launches: TodoMVC, SVGOMG, SVGOMG, TodoMVC; 60 original tests.
plan.instrumentation: Passive engine request spans plus an independent browser DevTools tracing session, started after native browser launch and fully drained before original browser shutdown. Actual tests and input remain on Flashwright. Only extra launch flag is remote-debugging-port=0 on loopback.
limitations: Trace durations are elapsed intervals, not CPU counters or removable time.
Trace buffering and hooks alter execution; these are not speed measurements.
Overlapping/nested events must be merged; timestamps require source/real calibration before cross-process overlap claims.
plan.retainedPredecessorFailure: Previous startup-trace capture passed 24 test bodies but lacked original browser-exit receipt and completed trace. Failed suite preserved; do not use it for timing or attribution.

analysis.scope: Union of measured request intervals, not CPU or a removable-cost estimate. Native clock shares original watchdog domain. Test bodies and selected recorded worker outcomes verified.

nativeIntervals.scope: Union of complete native trace event intervals across observed renderer main threads, intersected with current engine request intervals in a calibrated native clock. Temporal overlap is not causal ownership, CPU accounting or removable-time attribution. Nested names overlap and cannot be added; incomplete trace events remain unmeasured.

retainedFailedPredecessor.revision: Drain the diagnostics trace before original browser shutdown; keep production shutdown rules unchanged.

clock.scope: Same-host same-boot clock only; host/boot and ownership admission remain external

result.scope: Native JSON trace microsecond timestamps fall within original CLOCK_MONOTONIC request brackets, allowing 1 microsecond export quantization. Same host and browser build only.

separateInitialClockControl.scope: Small startup-trace calibration only; does not admit the failed application capture.

interpretation: In the two host-only full-capability TodoMVC runs, navigation occupies about 30% of complete-owner elapsed time, pointer requests about 20%, and text/control input about 11%. These are request intervals including waits, not removable costs.

In the two separately instrumented TodoMVC native traces, navigation spans about 1456 ms, overlaps 1213-1220 ms of complete renderer-main events and 747 ms of selected compiler/parsing/deserialization events. These sets overlap; do not add them.

Pointer request intervals include substantial time without observed complete renderer-main events. Browser/compositor work, IPC, scheduling, readiness and unrecorded events remain possible; absence of a selected event is not proof of idle or removable work.

Selected compiler events include source-position and lazy compilation work as well as initial parsing. This observation does not supersede previous cache, console-stack or eager-compilation negative screens.
No compiled coarse native action endpoint has been implemented or measured by this checkpoint. The current path still uses resident preparation plus native Input commands.
limitations: One worker, two applications and two orders; diagnostic instrumentation changes execution.
No comparison between traced and untraced elapsed times is admitted as a speed result.
Native traces start after browser launch and finish before browser close; startup and final shutdown are outside the native capture.
Only complete X events on observed CrRendererMain threads contribute to native unions. Other phases and threads are retained in raw traces but excluded from these intervals.
Temporal overlap is not causal ownership, CPU accounting, critical-path attribution or a removable-time bound. Nested event-name overlaps are nonadditive.
Clock calibration applies to this same-host, same-boot browser build with microsecond trace quantization.
Worker journals retain the previous selected enforcement scope; exact per-test native attribution, bounded long-suite recording, broader capabilities and production IPC remain unfinished.
Successful original browser waits and observed cleanup do not establish exhaustive resource custody or release acceptance.
decision: Preserve the positive painting-heavy result and negative combined-omission application screen separately. Do not repeat unchanged cache, frame-hint or omission screens. A native action experiment must measure a concrete implementation and preserve fresh stability, native input and completion semantics; these intervals alone do not predict its gain.
